headline: For first quarter, growth above 5%
content: The economic scenario for January seems tepid, experts indicate, but it should accelerate towards March. They agree that GDP during said month would show more dynamism due to seasonal reasons. This year, Easter holidays fall in April (the previous year were in March); thus, the third month of this year will have two additional working days translating into greater production. According to Oscar, the first-quarter growth could exceed 5%; he did not specify but mentioned around 5.7%. Last Year’s Closure On Friday last week, the economy grew 5.02% over the past year marking its third consecutive year of deceleration. Regarding December, it was important to note that seasonally adjusted GDP fell 0.4%. That means excluding calendar effects like Christmas, national production contracted compared to November. Juan Carlos Oscar acknowledged reflecting a weaker recovery than expected though nothing dramatic. He added that even holiday sales were below expectations.

headline: February inflation projected similarly to January
content: FebruarystoodareduplicateJanuarys rate where consumer price index rose 0.32%, estimates the central bank. Data from January almost doubled analysts’ forecasts leading annualized rates slightly beyond target range between 1%-3% reaching 3.07%. Typically early months see supply factors depending largely on climate conditions explained Adrián Armás, head of studies at the Reserve Bank. Despite favorable February business activity, similar trends to January anticipated. The central bank expects initial inflation near upper limit of targeted range owing delayed impact of supply shocks.

headline: Vehicle Sales Drop 7% in January
content: According to the Association of Automotive Representatives of Peru (ARP), vehicle sales dropped 7% in the country during the first month of the year compared to January 2013. Thus, ending January there were sold 14,379 vehicles versus 15,468 units previously. Decreased sales observed across most categories such as light-duty trucks, commercial vehicles, trailers down approximately 7%, except buses which increased by 6%. Toyota and Hyundai continued market leadership despite overall decline.

headline: Water Tariff Increase Request Denied Again
content: Despite efforts, water tariff increase request denied again by regulator SUNASS. headline: Galeras de Lima facturan hasta US$ 1,950 por metro cuadrado
content: Una buena parte de la clase media coquetea al mismo tiempo con los centros comerciales y las galerías. Hay aproximadamente 150 mil locales en las galerías de Lima. El 25% de puestos en los mercados ya no opera. Pese al incremento de los centros comerciales en el país, especialmente en Lima, existe un segmento de consumidores, ‘una parte de la clase media’, que también frecuenta el retail moderno, teniendo aún opciones como las denominadas ‘polvorillas’ o mejor conocidas como galerías, donde se aglutinan múltiples ofertas bajo un único concepto. No es necesario disponer de gran cantidad de metros cuadrados para vender exitosamente en estas entidades; lo crucial es seleccionar bien el rubro al cual dedicarse. Los rubros de computadoras y accesorios, belleza y deportes son quienes reportan mayores ingresos gracias a precios competitivos disponibles incluso en las galerías, permitiendo además aplicar técnicas tradicionales de venta como el regateo.

headline: Objetivo es tener el 7% del mercado este año
content: Después de destacar con su línea de excavadoras para minería y construcción durante el último semestre del 2013, Gildemeister Maquinarias aspira alcanzar el 7% de dicho mercado este año y lograr el 10% hacia el 2025. Su director señala que sólo en el 2013 colocaron 45 unidades de esos modelos de la marca SANY VALENCIANO, obteniendo así un 5% de penetración en el mercado. Además, planean expandirse introduciendo diversas líneas adicionales de maquinarias dirigidas a distintos sectores industriales.

headline: Entrevista: Parques de diversión apuestan por gestión de la novedad

Esta táctica resalta frente a la aparición de alternativas temporales, asegurando diferenciación y adaptación continua a las expectativas cambiantes de los visitantes.
